newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up after hitting new 6-yr low.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up after hitting new 6-yr low.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Tuesday after touching a new six-year low of 834.50 in the morning, traders said.
It was the lowest level for the won since South Korea introduced a market average system in March 1990.
The won ended at 832.80 after opening at 834.00. It peaked at 832.70.
The won lost strength in early morning in line with firmer dollar versus the Japanese yen in the world markets, traders said.
However, expected month-end export deals in the near future sparked dollar selling later, they said.
"Banks anticipate inflow of end-of-the-month export negotiations tomorrow," said one dealer. "So long dollar holders started squaring their positions."
Traders said the won was expected to trade in a range of 831 to 834 on Wednesday. The base mid-rate is seen at 833.60 compared with today's 831.10.
